EXAM NAME: Screening Mammography, Bilateral

REASON FOR EXAM / CLINICAL INDICATION:
Routine annual screening mammogram. Patient is asymptomatic with no new breast complaints. No personal history of breast cancer. Family history negative for premenopausal breast cancer.

TECHNIQUE:
Digital mammography was performed, consisting of craniocaudal (CC) and mediolateral oblique (MLO) views of both breasts. Computer-aided detection (CAD) was utilized.

COMPARISON STUDY:
Compared to prior mammogram dated 10/20/2022.

FINDINGS:
BREAST COMPOSITION: The breasts are heterogeneously dense, which may obscure small masses.
RIGHT BREAST: No suspicious masses, architectural distortion, or clustered microcalcifications are identified. Skin and subcutaneous tissues are unremarkable.
LEFT BREAST: No suspicious masses, architectural distortion, or clustered microcalcifications are identified. Skin and subcutaneous tissues are unremarkable.
AXILLAE: No axillary lymphadenopathy is noted bilaterally.

IMPRESSION:
1. No evidence of malignancy.
2. BI-RADS Category 1: Negative.
3. Routine annual screening mammogram recommended.
